what: Credicorp is Peru's largest financial group. It owns Banco de Crédito del Perú, the country's biggest bank, plus insurance, pension fund management, investment banking and the Yape mobile payments app used by most Peruvian adults.
customers: Peruvian households, small businesses and corporations, plus Bolivian, Chilean and Colombian clients.
money: Banco de Crédito deposits, lending and payments
Pacífico insurance and Prima pension funds
Mibanco lending to small and informal businesses
moat: The leading bank in a country where a few institutions hold most deposits, with Yape giving it a payments network that reaches far beyond its branch customers.
risks: Peruvian political instability has been persistent
Microfinance lending has higher loss rates in downturns
Commodity prices drive the Peruvian economy and therefore credit quality
opportunities: Net margin of 29% with return on equity among the highest of Latin American banks
Yape is turning a payments app into a lending and commerce platform
A dividend yield above 4% with analysts seeing about 24% upside
watch: Yape monetisation and the non-performing loan ratio in microfinance.
